Article Title: Tiger Shroff firing case: Oppn targets Fadnavis govt with 'jungle raj' claims
Article Text:
Tiger Shroff shooting incident: Opposition targets Maharashtra CM

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Opposition on Sunday targeted the Maharashtra government over the firing incident involving Bollywood actor Tiger Shroff in Mumbai’s Juhu area, alleging that the incident reflected a deteriorating law-and-order situation in the state.Shroff escaped unhurt after unidentified gunmen opened fire near Pushpa Park on Sunday evening. His driver and an autorickshaw driver sustained injuries in the incident, police said.The incident prompted sharp reactions from opposition leaders, who cited previous attacks and killings while questioning the government’s handling of public safety.Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Sanjay Raut directly blamed CM Devendra Fadnavis , who holds the home portfolio, for the state’s security situation. Referring to previous incidents involving Salman Khan, the murder of NCP leader Baba Siddique and the killing of Shiv Sena worker Pradeep Purnekar, Raut said the latest shooting reflected a wider breakdown in law and order.“Devendra Fadnavis is the Home Minister of this state. He is also Chief Minister, but the responsibility for maintaining law and order lies with him,” Raut said.Calling the situation “jungle raj”, he demanded the government’s dismissal and the imposition of President’s Rule.He also urged the Supreme Court to examine the broader situation, alleging that shootings, murders, extortion and kidnappings had become matters of serious concern.NCP (SP)MP Supriya Sule also raised concerns over public safety in a post on X, calling on the state’s home minister to review the law-and-order situation.“Shootings are continuously surfacing across the state, and the situation is such that criminals no longer fear the law,” Sule wrote.She added, “In broad daylight, on busy streets, criminals are brandishing swords and firing shots. This picture of the law and order situation in Maharashtra is extremely alarming.” Sule said citizens were increasingly anxious about their safety and urged the government to take measures to reassure the public.Maharashtra Congress president Harshwardhan Sapkal also accused the Mahayuti government of allowing 'jungle raj' in the state and demanded chief minister's resignation on moral grounds.In a post on X, Sapkal questioned the safety of ordinary citizens, asking, “If an actor like Tiger Shroff can be shot at in broad daylight in a metropolis like Mumbai, then who will guarantee the safety of ordinary citizens?”"Law and order in the state has completely broken down. Criminals no longer fear the law, and the Chief Minister's control over the police administration has ceased to exist", he said in a post on X.Meanwhile, an FIR has been registered against three unidentified persons under Sections 109(1) and 3(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), along with Sections 3 and 25 of the Arms Act.The Mumbai Police formed 15 teams to investigate the incident. Three men accused of involvement in the firing were arrested in Kota, Rajasthan earlier. Police are investigating the alleged roles of the accused and whether others were involved in planning or executing the attack.CM Fadnavis earlier said those responsible would be traced and would not be spared. Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde visited Shroff’s residence on Sunday night and assured the family of the government’s support.Shinde said, “Tiger suffered injuries to his left hand caused by gunpowder and glass fragments... Both the actor and his mother, Ayesha Shroff, were deeply shaken by the incident. Strict action will be taken, and threats against public figures will not be tolerated.”Investigators are also examining whether the shooting was planned after surveillance of Shroff’s movements.
Article Summary: Tiger Shroff escaped unhurt after gunmen opened fire near Pushpa Park on Sunday evening. Shiv Sena MP Sanjay Raut directly blamed CM Devendra Fadnavis for the state’s security situation. Raut said the latest shooting reflected a wider breakdown in law and order.

Article Title: ‘Shame on petty men’: Shashi Tharoor slams Centre’s silence Indian-origin Navanethem 'Navi' Pillay's Nobel win
Article Text:
Tharoor drew attention to Navi Pillay's ancestral roots

NEW DELHI: Senior Congress leader Shashi Tharoor on Sunday criticised the Union government for not congratulating this year’s Nobel Peace Prize laureate, Navanethem “Navi” Pillay, a South African jurist of Indian origin.The Thiruvananthapuram MP took to social media to question the government’s silence six days after Pillay won the award.“It’s been six days since this remarkable woman of Indian origin (see her story, attached) won the #NobelPeacePrize. And the Government of India, her ancestral homeland, hasn’t so much as congratulated her?! Shame on the petty men who have made such a deplorable decision,” Tharoor wrote on X.Without naming any leader from the ruling-BJP, Tharoor also drew attention to Pillay’s ancestral roots in Tamil Nadu.Navanethem “Navi” Pillay, a jurist at the International Court of Justice , was awarded the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize for her efforts to promote peace and international law by ensuring that war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide are prosecuted.
Article Summary: Senior Congress leader Shashi Tharoor criticised the Union government for not congratulating this year’s Nobel Peace Prize laureate, Navanethem ‘Navi’ Pillay. The Thiruvananthapuram MP took to social media to question the government's silence six days after Pillay won the award.

Article Title: Shinde meets Tiger Shroff after firing incident; pics show actor with bandages
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Maharashtra deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde met Bollywood actor Tiger Shroff at his residence on Sunday night after a firing incident in Mumbai's Juhu area, assuring the actor and his family of the state government's support. Photographs from the meeting showed Shroff with bandages on his arm and dressings on his shoulder and chest.Speaking to reporters after the meeting, Shinde said five rounds had been fired during the incident, but the actor was safe. He added that Shroff had sustained injuries to his left hand due to gunpowder and glass shards, while his driver was injured in the incident.Also Read: Tiger Shroff covers face, reaches home under police protection after Juhu firing; tape on hand draws attention "This is a major incident... five rounds were fired, but fortunately, he was safe. His driver sustained injuries, and the incident is condemnable. I met with the actor; he has injuries on his left hand caused by gunpowder and shards of glass. Both he and his mother are quite shaken... I have assured them that the state government stands with them in the face of the open threats being directed at public figures... No form of threat will be tolerated," Shinde said.Shinde visited the actor to enquire about his well-being after reports of gunshots being fired while Shroff was leaving a football club on Sunday evening.His mother, Ayesha Shroff, was also present during the meeting. Actor Disha Patani later arrived at Shroff's residence.Also Read: New video captures Tiger Shroff's assassination bid: 3 men, 7 shots fired, gun jams before 6th Condemning the firing, Shinde said the state government would not tolerate attempts to intimidate public figures and assured the Shroff family that the authorities would take necessary steps to address the threat.Drawing a comparison with the gang-related violence witnessed in Mumbai in the 1990s, the deputy chief minister said the police had brought such activities under control and vowed to prevent their resurgence."Such gang wars were quite common in the 90s, but the Mumbai Police put an end to them in 1995... These attempts to intimidate people will not be tolerated, and we will put an end to this hooliganism," he said.Shinde's visit came amid concerns over the firing incident, with the state government assuring the actor and his family of its support. The police have maintained that Shroff was safe and had not suffered any gunshot wounds.

SRINAGAR: The J&K govt and political parties in the union territory have unitedly condemned the attack on a Srinagar-bound bus in Haryana.According to a govt spokesperson, CM Omar Abdullah’s office has conveyed its concern to the Haryana govt, which has assured prompt and stringent action.“This unfortunate incident should never have taken place. Article Title: 'Laal Hit Janta Party': New outfit emerges to counter CJP's protests against CEC Gyanesh Kumar
Article Text:
Lal hit janta party held a meeting in Delhi and called for constitutional values, accountability and responsible participation in protests

NEW DELHI: As the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) intensifies its campaign demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation, a group calling itself the Laal Hit Janta Party has emerged as a satirical counter to the outfit.At a meeting in the national capital on Sunday, the outfit called for constitutional values, accountability and responsible public participation, while reiterating its opposition to the CJP's demonstrations, according to a statement issued by the organisation.The outfit urged young citizens, particularly Gen Z, to engage in democratic processes through peaceful protests, factual communication and legal channels. Its motto is: “Nation First, Respect for the Constitution, Democracy as Our Identity,” while its guiding principle is: “Strong in Opposition, Peaceful in Action, Committed to the Nation.”According to news agency PTI, the meeting was held at Malviya Smriti Bhawan on Pandit Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Marg and was addressed by convenor Ayan Bhatnagar and filmmakers Richa Gupta, Pawan Nagpal and Atul Gangwar.The group's name appears to be a satirical reference to a popular insect-control brand, mirroring the CJP's name.The outfit had earlier held a gathering at Janpath, where around 200 people assembled to denounce alleged assaults on police personnel and abusive language directed at Prime Minister Narendra Modi during protests.Speaking to IANS, Bhatnagar had said the group was not formed to challenge the CJP through public debate."The Lal Hit Janta Party was not formed to contest elections, as we have already made clear. We stand against CJP and its protests. We oppose cockroaches who want to weaken the country's democracy and attempt to create anarchy in the country," he said."We will gather in different groups, on both large and small scales, present our views and arguments, and take our message forward. We will show them that a party like the 'Lal HIT Janta Party' now exists to challenge them. If you have the courage, come and debate," Bhatnagar added.In its statement on Sunday's meeting, the organisation said political debate over electoral processes should be based on verified evidence, transparent procedures and constitutional mechanisms. It also stressed the importance of preserving the independence and credibility of constitutional institutions, including the Election Commission, amid calls for Kumar's resignation.These developments come against the backdrop of widespread demonstrations against the CEC regarding alleged irregularities in electoral roll revisions. The protesters, including opposition parties, the CJP and several student groups have claimed that the exercise led to the deletion of lakhs of voters’ names and raised questions over changes to Form 6, which is used to register as a voter. These allegations, however, remain subject to verification.The counter-outfit called for questions about political organisations, their funding and alleged links to unlawful activities to be examined through verified documents, lawful investigations and official findings.
Article Summary: Lal hit janta party held a meeting in Delhi and called for constitutional values, accountability and responsible participation in protests. The group's name appears to be a satirical reference to a popular insect-control brand, mirroring the CJP's name.

Article Title: Tiger Shroff shooting: The Salman Khan connection and a trail of threats linked to Lawrence Bishnoi
Article Text:
Tiger Shroff firing revives focus on Bishnoi gang’s threats against Salman Khan

Why has Salman Khan been mentioned?

Threats against Salman Khan over the years

Firing outside Salman Khan's home in 2024

Baba Siddique murder and Rohit Shetty firing

What happens next in the Tiger Shroff case?

NEW DELHI: Gangster Lawrence Bishnoi 's long-running feud with Salman Khan brought actor Tiger Shroff into the spotlight on Sunday after gunmen opened fire at his car in Mumbai's Juhu. Seven rounds were fired in the incident, but the actor escaped without bullet injuries.Shroff's driver, Firdaus, and another person were injured in the October 18 attack, which prompted a police investigation into the identity of the assailants and their motive.A message attributed to the Bishnoi gang claimed responsibility for the firing and linked it to Shroff's association with superstar Salman Khan. The message also warned others in the film industry against working with Salman.The attack is the latest in a series of incidents involving threats and violence allegedly linked to the Bishnoi network against Bollywood personalities and others associated with Salman Khan.The Bishnoi gang's message after the incident linked the attack to Tiger Shroff's professional association with Salman Khan. It claimed that Shroff had been warned earlier but had ignored the warning.The message stated: "Anyone in the Mumbai film industry who does not listen to us or works with Salman Khan will be next."In an audio message released after the attack, a man identified as Anil Pandit threatened Salman Khan and his family, warning the actor against relying on his security and demanding an apology to Lawrence Bishnoi and the Bishnoi community."Listen to me carefully, Salman Khan. If you don't apologise to my elder brother, Lawrence Bishnoi, or to the Bishnoi community, then we won't even leave a dog in your house. We will destroy your entire family. Keep this in mind. Don't think that you are in security and nothing will happen to you," Pandit said in the audio message.The message also warned rival gang members against using the group's name to gain attention. It appeared to be aimed at intimidating not just Shroff but others in the film industry who work with Salman Khan.The authenticity of the messages and the gang's claimed role in the attack remain subject to police verification.The dispute involving the Bajrangi Bhaijaan actor dates back to the 1998 blackbuck poaching case. Lawrence Bishnoi has repeatedly threatened the actor over the case, citing the blackbuck's religious significance to the Bishnoi community.The threats against Salman Khan have continued for years.In June 2022, a threat letter was reportedly found at Bandra Bandstand, where the actor's father, Salim Khan, used to go for walks.The letter warned that Salman Khan would meet the same fate as Punjabi singer Sidhu Moosewala, who was murdered in May that year.In March 2023, Salman Khan's manager received a threatening email referring to Lawrence Bishnoi's threats against the actor. The email also mentioned Goldy Brar, a Canada-based gangster and a close associate of Lawrence Bishnoi.On April 14, 2024, two motorcycle-borne men opened fire outside Salman Khan's Galaxy Apartments residence in Bandra. The actor was not injured.Mumbai Police alleged that the shooting was carried out at the behest of the Bishnoi gang. Anmol Bishnoi, Lawrence's brother and a close associate, was among those wanted in connection with the case.Investigators examined the roles of the alleged shooters and their associates, including how the attack was planned.In a separate case, Navi Mumbai Police filed a chargesheet in 2024 alleging that members of the gang had been offered Rs 25 lakh to attack Salman Khan.According to the police, the plan included targeting him during a film shoot or while he was travelling to his Panvel farmhouse.The case also highlighted the role of people allegedly involved in surveillance and planning, beyond those who directly carried out an attack.The threats surrounding Salman drew further attention after former Maharashtra minister Baba Siddique was shot dead on October 12, 2024.Siddique, a three-time MLA and Nationalist Congress Party leader, was killed outside the office of his son, Zeeshan Siddique, in Bandra East.A social media post linked to the Bishnoi gang claimed responsibility for the murder and warned those helping Salman Khan. Police investigated the alleged links.On February 1, 2026, gunmen opened fire outside filmmaker Rohit Shetty's residence in Juhu.A post attributed to people linked to the Bishnoi network claimed responsibility and threatened further violence if its demands were ignored.Mumbai Police and the Crime Branch investigated the shooting, including the suspected attackers and their alleged links to the network.How the Bishnoi network operatesThe Lawrence Bishnoi network's alleged modus operandi involves different people handling the planning and execution of attacks.Police investigations have examined suspected surveillance, recruitment of shooters, weapons supply, communication between associates, and arrangements for transport and escape.In the 2024 case involving Salman, police alleged that the attackers had gathered information about the actor's movements and locations over an extended period. Investigators also looked into the roles of several people suspected of helping plan the attack.The network led by jailed gangster Lawrence Bishnoi has also been linked to attacks beyond India, including incidents in Canada and the UK.These include multiple shootings at comedian Kapil Sharma's cafe in Canada, which drew attention to the gang's overseas reach.In November 2025, news agency PTI reported that the National Investigation Agency arrested Anmol Bishnoi after his deportation from the United States.He was wanted in cases including the murder of Baba Siddique and the firing outside Salman Khan's residence.Anmol is Lawrence Bishnoi's brother and a close associate.Mumbai Police are investigating the firing to identify the attackers and establish the motive.Officers are examining CCTV footage and forensic evidence, while checking the authenticity of messages attributed to Anil Pandit and Harman Sandhu.Investigators are also looking into whether Shroff had received any threats before the incident.The probe will need to establish whether the attackers acted on behalf of an organised group or whether someone claimed responsibility after the shooting to exploit the incident.For now, the alleged Bishnoi gang link remains under investigation.
Article Summary: Gangster Lawrence Bishnoi's long-running feud with Salman Khan brought actor Tiger Shroff into the spotlight on Sunday. Seven rounds were fired in the incident, but the actor escaped without bullet injuries. A message attributed to the Bish noi gang claimed responsibility for the firing and linked it to Shroroff's association with superstar Salman Khan.

Article Title: Espionage case on Army officer’s wife, lens on ‘China links’
Article Text:
(Image used for representational purposes)

JAMMU: J&K Police have filed a case and started a probe against a Jammu-based Army officer’s wife for allegedly collecting and sharing sensitive information with foreign intelligence operatives, including those linked to China, sources said Sunday.The woman is from Telangana, works as a freelance researcher and had a UN internship in 2023. She allegedly used AI tools ChatGPT and Claude to write papers on sensitive security issues for Chinese intelligence operatives suspected to have contacted her posing as academicians. The information was allegedly passed on through encrypted communication (online) mediums.The woman married the major-rank officer in 2023, a year after finishing a course in international governance from Geneva. She got a Master’s degree from a Bengaluru university in 2021.A joint team of officers, including some from a central intelligence agency, intercepted the woman at Jammu railway station on Oct 14 when she was reportedly preparing to board a train to Pathankot. She was stopped and taken to a nearby military station for questioning, officials said. This followed a case filed at Jammu’s Gandhi Nagar Police Station under Official Secrets Act, and BNS sections relating to criminal conspiracy and offences against national sovereignty.A DSP assigned to lead the probe has questioned the woman, seizing her phone and extracting data that purportedly showed documents on sensitive subjects. The accused claimed her material was based entirely on open-source research supplemented by the AI platforms.The officials made it clear that despite being booked, the woman has not been arrested yet. Her interrogation indicated that she had interacted with several foreign nationals during her UN internship, including a Chinese national with whom she allegedly maintained contact through WhatsApp, the officials said. In 2024, she was in contact via social media with a Malaysian consultant allegedly working for Chinese intelligence agencies, the officials added.Preliminary investigations indicate the Chinese operatives initially made the woman write articles on environmental and geopolitics issues before gradually goading her to switch to defence matters. Investigators suspect she may have fallen into an “intellectual trap”, not realising that those approaching her as academicians were actually operatives trying to extract sensitive information.Investigators are examining whether the woman engaged in systematic information-sharing under the guise of freelance research, adding a comprehensive forensic examination of her digital devices and financial transactions is on to establish the exact nature of the shared material, the officials said.(With inputs from agencies)
Article Summary: The woman is from Telangana, works as a freelance researcher and had a UN internship in 2023. She allegedly used AI tools ChatGPT and Claude to write papers on sensitive security issues for Chinese intelligence operatives. The information was allegedly passed on through encrypted communication (online) mediums.

Article Title: Sudden rain, poor crowd management likely led to Kolkata Durga Puja stampede: What we know so far
Article Text:
Locals blame sudden rain, narrow space and lack of police personnel for stampede

High-level committee reviews pandals

Accused sent to 10-day police custody

Victims' bodies handed over to kin

12 patients likely to be discharged on Monday

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Amit Shah visits injured

NEW DELHI: At least 19 people died and 25 others were injured in a stampede at Kolkata's Chorbagan Durga Puja pandal on Saturday evening.The stampede occurred after a sudden downpour triggered a crowd surge, with hundreds of visitors rushing into the pandal for shelter and trapping those already inside.West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari blamed the incident on the organisers' callousness and appealed to puja committees across Kolkata to adopt safety measures.“It’s a painful incident and extremely heartbreaking,” Adhikari said.“As per initial information received, the incident happened due to an announcement made by the puja committee. Right now our priority is to treat the 25 people who have been injured. Among them, 24 are stable but one is critical. We are standing by the affected families. The Chorbagan puja pandal has been handed over to forensic teams, STF and fire brigade,” he added.Adhikari has also sought the list of temporary home guards deployed at the puja pandal to investigate their role in the stampede."These home guards are not new recruits. They were on duty for the third year in a row, following their earlier appointments in 2024 and 2025," he said."We are carrying on our shoulders a massive pile of rubbish as baggage. A clean-up will take time," Adhikari asserted.He pointed out that one of the home guards he tried to talk to at the pandal early this morning "could not even understand, let alone speak, Bengali".Here's what we know so far about the incident.Locals, who were among the first responders, said sudden rainfall, narrow lanes, a heavy rush of visitors and a lack of adequate volunteers and police personnel for crowd management contributed to the stampede.They said heavy rain forced people inside the pandal to wait for the weather to improve, while visitors outside grew restless and tried to rush into the already crowded marquee.Pramod Gupta, who lives near the Chorbagan puja pandal on Radha Madhav Lane, said the queue of visitors to the marquee had stretched to Mahatma Gandhi Road, about 700 metres away."Everything was fine till the rain started," he told news agency PTI."Standing in front of my house, I could hear screams as people rushed out. I and my daughters helped four girls and asked them to stay in our house till the situation eased," he said.Locals also said narrow lanes and a lack of police personnel and volunteers inside the pandal hampered the swift rescue of the injured."Ambulances could not reach the spot, and the injured had to be carried out to the main thoroughfare some distance away," a woman told PTI."We started the rescue work by breaking the bamboo structures and barricades of the pandal," another local man alleged.A high-level committee formed to review safety arrangements at major Durga Puja marquees across West Bengal began visiting community puja pandals on Sunday.The panel includes disaster management secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh and director general of fire services Anuj Sharma.The panel members will visit several crowd-puller Durga Puja pandals across Kolkata to review safety and security norms and crowd management plans, sources told PTI.The administration has stressed the need for wider exit points, adequate lighting and the removal of bottlenecks caused by temporary rope enclosures.Kolkata Police have arrested seven people, including organisers of the Chorbagan Durga Puja, a senior officer said.Police have also registered a suo motu case of culpable homicide not amounting to murder."We have arrested seven people. They were among the 14 detained last night. More arrests may be made," the IPS officer told PTI."Rajkumar Seoda and Shantanu Dubey were the secretary and vice-president, respectively, of the Chorbagan Puja committee. Biplab Mukhopadhyay was responsible for installing the bamboo structure at the pandal, while Kaushik Saha and Pintu De were in charge of crowd management," the officer said.Those arrested include the puja committee's secretary and vice-president, as well as two employees of a private security agency, among others, he said.The Bankshal Court remanded accused to 10 days of police custody. Police had sought 14 days of custody.Defence lawyer MD Yashim Raheman claimed that the accused were outsiders who had come to witness the Puja celebrations.He said the court had granted custody until October 28, while police had sought remand until November 1."We informed the court that these individuals were outsiders; they had come to witness the Durga Puja celebrations. Upon observing the heavy crowding--where many people were in distress--they stepped in to assist with rescue efforts...Regarding the police custody (PC), the court has granted it until the 28th. Everyone has been remanded to police custody until the 28th. The police had requested custody until the 1st, but the judge granted it until the 28th," he told news agency ANI.Authorities handed over the bodies of those killed in the stampede to their family members on Sunday.Among the victims was a 27-year-old nurse whose mortal remains were taken to her native place in Hooghly. Her relative told news agency ANI that she had gone to the pandal after completing her duty."After doing her duty, she went to watch the puja (worship/festival) with her friend," he said.The West Bengal government has announced compensation of Rs 25 lakh and a job for the family of each deceased person. The Special Task Force (STF) has also initiated an investigation to establish accountability.Twelve of the 14 patients admitted to Apollo Hospital in Salt Lake following the stampede are stable, with most expected to be discharged on Monday, Dr Narayan Banerjee said.Providing an update on the patients' condition, Dr Banerjee told ANI that five were in the Intensive Care Unit (ICU), while the remaining patients were being treated in the ward. He added that two patients continued to require closer monitoring.“Amit Shah ji came; it's a very good thing because the government has done whatever is possible. Except for two patients, all the others are stable. Of the 14 patients admitted, five are in the ICU, and the rest are in the ward," Dr Banerjee said."I think most of them will be discharged tomorrow, and a few who require surgery will remain here. Except for one patient who has a fractured pelvis and urethra, the others do not have very serious injuries or internal injuries so far. A young child, aged 13, was also admitted. She is fine,” he added.Union home minister Amit Shah and Suvendu Adhikari visited the injured undergoing treatment at Apollo Hospital earlier on Sunday.Shah had earlier expressed condolences to the families of those killed, describing the stampede as “extremely distressing”. He also said he had spoken to Adhikari to take stock of the situation.Following the incident, Kolkata Police imposed prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023, in parts of the city from October 18 to October 20 to maintain law and order and prevent untoward incidents.The order was issued amid concerns over possible demonstrations, rallies and meetings that could affect public order and safety.
Article Summary: At least 19 people died and 25 others were injured in a stampede at Kolkata's Chorbagan Durga Puja pandal on Saturday evening. The stampede occurred after a sudden downpour triggered a crowd surge, with hundreds of visitors rushing into the pandal for shelter. Locals, who were among the first responders, said sudden rainfall, narrow lanes, a heavy rush of visitors and a lack of adequate volunteers and police personnel contributed to the stampede.

Article Title: CJP's Dipke accuses state of delaying proceedings to prevent release of Saurav Das, Ashutosh Ranka
Article Text:
Dipke claims Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka's arrest being deliberately prolonged (Photo: PTI).

NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke on Sunday accused the state of intentionally prolonging Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka's arrest in order to delay court proceedings and delay their release."The state is deliberately prolonging Ashu and Saurav’s illegal arrest by using every dirty trick in the book to delay court proceedings and prevent their release," Dipke said in an X post."They have no legal grounds to keep them behind bars, so they are resorting to delaying tactics to keep them there," he added.On October 14, Das and Ranka were sent to five days of judicial custody after they entered Jantar Mantar, a site denotified for designated protest, by scaling its locked gates. The CJP leaders said they had unfurled the national flag and raised slogans.CJP's legal head Ratna Singh, who was present in the court for hearing on the matter accused the Special Executive Magistrate of "arbitrary remarks" and deliberately delaying the hearing, PTI reported."We have been here since morning. From that point onwards, the entire discussion was focused solely on the message."It is clear that this entire episode was orchestrated," Singh alleged, "They had decided beforehand to come into the courtroom and focus exclusively on this alleged threatening message, completely bypassing whether the formalities required for Saurav and Ashutosh's release were fulfilled."There was no response from police on the allegations yet. Article Title: Almost a century after J&K HC was set up, Ladakh gets bench
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Almost a century after the establishment of Jammu & Kashmir HC, the Union Territory of Ladakh Sunday got a high court bench, which will sit in Leh, 3,500 metres above sea level — an altitude no other HC can ever match.Inaugurating the Ladakh bench of J&K HC, CJI Surya Kant said, “I am told no HC in our country has ever sat higher. Of course, what matters today is not how high this court sits. What is important is how close it now stands to the people it serves.”J&K HC came into existence on March 26, 1928, with three judges, including Chief Justice Lala Kanwar Sein.Speaking on the evolution of the justice delivery system in Ladakh in the presence of HC Chief Justice Pushpendra Kumar Bhati and SC judges, CJI Kant said given the difficult terrain and harsh winter, approaching the court was more arduous than the cost of litigation for many. Only after Ladakh became a UT in 2019 was J&K HC rechristened HC of J&K and Ladakh.“But a name on a court’s letterhead is not the same as a court on one’s doorstep… The high court has today crossed the passes to reach Ladakh, instead of asking the people of Ladakh to cross the passes to reach it,” he said, appreciating the efforts of Union govt and Lt Governor V K Saxena, who was present at the ceremony along with attorney general R Venkataramani.But even establishing an HC bench at Leh would not take justice to the doorstep of far-flung villages in the region, the CJI said, advocating liberal use of technology and legal aid services.“Access to justice, after all, begins not in the court’s compound, but at the litigant’s door. The law places this duty on the HC as well, through its legal services committee, and I am confident that, working... with the legal services authority, it will discharge that responsibility by reaching every door in Ladakh where justice is still awaited,” he said.In an unprecedented gesture, the CJI said, “Once video-conferencing facilities are adequately available to the lawyers of the Ladakh bench, Supreme Court shall list all matters coming from Ladakh on a single day, and hear them on a day-to-day basis, also through videoconferencing.”“Somewhere in Ladakh today, in a classroom in Kargil or Nubra, there is a young child who will one day argue her first case in this court, and perhaps even sit on its bench as a judge. When that day comes, we will know that this bench has not merely arrived in Ladakh but taken root here,” the CJI said.
Article Summary: J&K HC came into existence on March 26, 1928, with three judges, including Chief Justice Lala Kanwar Sein. CJI Surya Kant: “I am told no HC in our country has ever sat higher.”

MUMBAI: A series of videos has emerged showing the firing incident involving Bollywood actor Tiger Shroff in Mumbai’s Juhu area, including footage capturing the moments when unidentified assailants opened fire at his car and the actor switched seats to take the wheel after his driver was injured.The incident took place around 7 pm on Sunday near Pushpa Narsee Park, also known as Jamnabai Nursery, where Shroff was leaving after attending a birthday party. Seven shots were fired at the vehicle, injuring his driver, Firdaus, and a passerby identified as Umesh Charan.One of the videos circulating on social media captures the firing incident, with three men involved in the attack. Two of the assailants approached the vehicle on foot while a third waited on a motorcycle to facilitate their escape.The attackers opened fire as Shroff’s car was slowly moving out of the venue. Shroff and Firdaus were subsequently taken to Nanavati Hospital in Vile Parle for medical attention.The footage provides a glimpse of the immediate aftermath of the firing, as those present at the scene reacted to the incident.Shroff escaped without any bullet injuries, although he sustained minor abrasions from shattered glass. His driver suffered a gunshot wound to his left hand, while Charan sustained bullet injuries to his chest. Both were taken to hospital for treatment.In another purported video that went viral on social media, the gun appears to jam as the shooter attempts to fire the sixth shot. The other shooter then fires two more rounds, taking the total number of shots fired to seven.The Lawrence Bishnoi gang has been linked to claims of responsibility for the shooting through a social media post and a voice note attributed to individuals identifying themselves as Anil Pandit and Harman Sandhu. Police are verifying these claims and investigating the motive behind the attack.Also read - 'Apologise to Lawrence Bishnoi': After Tiger Shroff attack, fresh warning to Salman Khan in chilling audio MEanwhile, doctors said Charan was stable but required surgery. Firdaus was also being treated for his gunshot injury.An eyewitness who was present in the area described how the assailants positioned themselves before opening fire at Shroff’s vehicle.Rakesh Kumar, an autorickshaw driver, told ANI that three individuals were involved in the incident. According to his account, one person was on a motorcycle while two others were standing outside, with one near the gate and another positioned slightly ahead of it.Recalling the sequence of events, Kumar said, "I drive a rickshaw here in Mumbai... I arrived around 7:00 PM to take my vehicle out... There were three individuals involved: one was on a motorcycle, while two others were standing outside - one near the gate, and another positioned slightly ahead of it. When the shooting began, one person opened fire from the front, targeting the specific seat where Tiger Shroff was sitting. .. another person, the one near the gate, fired a shot that struck the driver in the hand. It happened around 7:00 PM..."Mumbai Police have formed 15 teams to investigate the shooting and identify those involved. Juhu police and the Mumbai Crime Branch are examining CCTV footage from the area to establish the suspects’ movements and escape route.The three assailants fled towards SV Road and Vile Parle railway station on a motorcycle. Police are also investigating whether Shroff had received any threats before the attack.The motive behind the shooting remains under investigation.Also Read: 'Apologise to Lawrence Bishnoi': After Tiger Shroff attack, fresh warning to Salman Two individuals identifying themselves as Anil Pandit and Harman Sandhu, and claiming links to the Lawrence Bishnoi gang, purportedly took responsibility for the attack through a social media post and a voice note.The message alleged that Shroff had ignored warnings and also threatened people in the film industry who continued to work with actor Salman Khan.Police are verifying the authenticity of the claims and investigating whether the individuals who issued the threats were connected to the shooting. Their claims of responsibility have not been independently established.The incident has prompted concerns over the security of film personalities in Mumbai, following previous firing incidents targeting Salman Khan’s residence and other attacks linked to alleged gang rivalries.Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis spoke to Mumbai Police Commissioner Deven Bharti to seek an update on the investigation and directed the police to take strict action against those responsible.Fadnavis also spoke to Shroff and assured him, “We are all with you. Article Title: Congress’s post-truth politics: Manufacturing distrust, undermining democracy
Article Text:
For nearly seven decades, Congress govts retained executive control over appointment of CEC

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Rajnath Singh is the minister of defence, Government of India.

It is said that often truth is the first casualty of war. This is increasingly becoming true of political contests as well, where post-truth politics is emerging as an important dimension of public discourse.In the post-truth scenario, false propaganda, distorted narratives, and emotional appeals devoid of logic often take precedence over objective facts and verifiable evidence. And, reasoned debate gives way to demagoguery.Once largely a subject of academic debates, post-truth has now become a feature of everyday politics. Misinformation campaigns designed to gaslight are increasingly used to not only sway public opinion but also discredit democratic institutions.Allegations are repeated and amplified even when the evidence to substantiate them is conspicuously absent. In this, truth seems to be not merely the first casualty, but it risks becoming the final casualty as well.India’s political discourse is not immune to this post-truth phenomenon. Increasingly, sections of the opposition parties appear to be manufacturing outrage, peddling propaganda and weaponising misinformation to spread anarchy, placing avaricious political goals above national interests.The article does not aim a jeremiad against the opposition nor a claim that constitutional institutions are beyond criticism. Dissent is the lifeblood of democracy. What it is not is a licence to peddle falsehoods. Disagreement is necessary for better policymaking. What it is not is a pass for vindictive and sustained assault on public trust through allegations that crumble under factual scrutiny.The purpose, therefore, is to challenge these falsehoods and restore public trust in constitutional institutions, which has been eroded by the cynical politics of manufactured distrust.This becomes particularly significant when we examine how electoral institutions and processes have been attacked by certain sections of opposition to hide the fact that people are rejecting them again and again.Three issues, in particular, stand out: the recurring allegations of manipulation of Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs), the controversy surrounding the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and unscrupulous attempts to discredit the Election Commission of India (ECI).First things first, EVMs have repeatedly been subjected to allegations of manipulation by the opposition. The Supreme Court has examined such challenges on multiple occasions. Finally, in 2024, in its ‘Association for Democratic Reforms v. Election Commission of India’, the Supreme Court put to rest all doubts and rejected demands for a return to paper ballots. The Supreme Court observed that repeated challenges based on suspicion and doubt, without cogent material or data, were “execrable and undesirable”. But this could not stop the opposition from repeating the same lies again and again.The controversy surrounding the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls is another example of how a legally right and administratively justified exercise has been impugned for narrow political interests by some in this post-truth era.In 2025, the Supreme Court in its ‘Association for Democratic Reforms v. Election Commission of India’ judgment, affirmed that the integrity of electoral rolls is foundational to free and fair elections. It described the objective of ensuring the “accuracy, completeness, and integrity of the electoral roll” as “not only legitimate but is integral to the constitutional mandate” entrusted to the Commission.The Court also found that the reasons advanced for the revision bore a “direct and rational nexus” to maintaining a credible electoral process. These observations reinforced a fundamental principle: protecting the right to vote requires not only safeguarding every eligible voter, but also ensuring that electoral rolls remain accurate, complete and reliable.Beyond EVMs and SIR, a sustained campaign has been run to discredit the office of the Chief Election Commissioner, and by extension the institution of the Election Commission of India (ECI).For nearly seven decades, Congress governments retained executive control over the appointment of Chief Election Commissioner. Our government changed this by institutionalising the appointment process through a multi-member Selection Committee that includes the Leader of the Opposition.The record of Congress has been far from inspiring when it comes to respecting the independence of other constitutional institutions as well.In 1951, the then government introduced the First Constitutional Amendment to reverse Supreme Court judgment and curtailed freedom of speech and expression.During the Emergency, constitutional amendments were weaponised to serve the interests of the government. The amendments made the proclamation of Emergency non-justiciable and placed the Prime Minister’s election beyond judicial scrutiny. It also granted sweeping immunity to high constitutional functionaries and curtailed judicial review. The amendment power was turned from an instrument of constitutional reform into a tool for executive aggrandisement.Not only institutions were trampled but human rights of citizens were also violated. Attorney General Niren De, representing the then Union Government, argued in the Supreme Court that even if an innocent person was killed by a police officer acting out of personal enmity, the victim’s family could not seek judicial relief.Now, compare this with how the Constitution has been honoured in the last 12 years under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi. The 99th Constitutional Amendment Act, passed by a special majority of Parliament, was struck down by the Supreme Court. The verdict was not only respected, but no attempt was made to overturn it through backdoor legislation. This respect for the Constitution and its principles has also guided our approach to some of the most consequential issues facing the nation.The construction of the Ram Mandir began only after the Supreme Court’s judgment. When Article 370 was abrogated and the Supreme Court upheld the decision, many in the opposition still disagreed with the judgment.Even legislative processes and offices have not been spared by the Congress. A no-confidence motion was moved against the Lok Sabha Speaker when he simply asked the Leader of opposition to follow the rules.Post-truth politics has also extended to matters of national security. In 2019, the Congress leader wrongly attributed a slogan to the Supreme Court’s Rafale judgment and later tendered an unconditional apology in contempt proceedings. In August 2025, the Supreme Court again questioned the basis of claims made by Rahul Gandhi regarding the occupation of Indian territory, asking what credible evidence supported them.Respecting differences of opinion has always been an integral part of our democratic ethos. When people raised concerns over the three farm laws passed by Parliament, we not only listened to those concerns but also repealed the laws in the larger public interest.In a democracy, one is free to disagree with a decision. But such disagreements cannot be founded on falsehoods, nor can their purpose be to create disorder and anarchy. Dr. B. R. Ambedkar, in his famous speech in the Constituent Assembly, often referred to as the “Grammar of Anarchy,” warned against the dangers of resorting to unconstitutional methods.His message remains profoundly relevant today. Opposition leaders would do well to read this historic speech and understand the crucial distinction between dissent and anarchy in a democracy.We believe that the foundation of a vibrant democracy lies not merely in political equality, but also in economic and social justice. This principle underpins the decisions taken by our government.At the same time, for a stable and mature democracy it is important that dissent and concerns be expressed through legitimate and democratic channels, and resolved through dialogue and mutual understanding rather than by resorting to disorder.The need of the hour is to ensure that neither our democratic institutions nor India’s rise are held hostage to the frustration arising from political defeats. And, at no cost will the nation's progress be allowed to be undermined by those who would rather discredit the system than confront the reasons for their own setbacks.
Article Summary: Once largely a subject of academic debates, post-truth has now become a feature of everyday politics. Misinformation campaigns designed to gaslight are increasingly used to sway public opinion and discredit democratic institutions. For nearly seven decades, Congress govts retained executive control over appointment of CEC.

NEW DELHI: Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav on Sunday accused the BJP of conspiring to manipulate electoral rolls by adding bogus votes and deleting genuine votes of opposition supporters, urging party workers to remain vigilant at their respective polling booths ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections.Addressing party leaders and workers from various districts at the SP headquarters in Lucknow, the former Uttar Pradesh chief minister alleged that the BJP was resorting to electoral malpractice to win elections and disregarding the Constitution.In a statement released by the party, Yadav said, "BJP is conspiring to add fake votes to electoral rolls. Party workers should remain vigilant at their respective polling booths. The BJP considers fake votes and dishonesty its strength. It resorts to different types of electoral manoeuvres, including getting fake votes added to electoral rolls and genuine votes of opposition parties deleted."He urged people to remain alert against what he described as "vote theft and donation theft".Yadav's allegations come days after he questioned the rationale behind the Election Commission's Special Summary Revision (SSR) of electoral rolls.He had said the Samajwadi Party was not opposed to either the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) or SSR, but would resist any alleged attempt to manipulate voter lists to benefit the BJP."When the Election Commission of India spent thousands of crores of rupees and completed the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls a couple of months ago, what is the need for SSR?" praharis to assist voters with the revision exercise at the booth level.Apart from electoral issues, Yadav criticised the BJP government's record in Uttar Pradesh, citing inflation, unemployment, corruption, alleged misuse of public funds, injustice and atrocities as concerns affecting people.He accused the ruling party of protecting land grabbers and alleged that people associated with the BJP were encroaching on land belonging to poor and vulnerable sections of society, as well as government land.Yadav further claimed that people approaching authorities for justice were being implicated in cases and that the police often sided with influential BJP supporters.He asserted that public support for a Samajwadi Party government was growing and expressed confidence that voters Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak (backward classes, Dalits and minorities), was united and alleged that the BJP government and the chief minister were targeting its members because of their unity.Yadav accused the BJP government of weakening Uttar Pradesh's education system, claiming that more than 26,000 primary schools had been shut down over the past decade while the number of liquor shops had increased.He alleged that corruption and exploitation had harmed school education and that teachers, educational institutions, graduates and young people faced discrimination.The SP chief also claimed that Uttar Pradesh had recorded the highest number of examination paper leaks in the country, accusing the state government of failing to ensure the integrity of recruitment and other examinations.In his earlier remarks, Yadav had also alleged that concerns over voter-list manipulation extended across generations, saying that young people were raising questions about the electoral process.He additionally criticised the BJP's proposed 'One Nation, One Election' plan, alleging that it could allow the party to consolidate control over governments across the country and avoid accountability through repeated elections.Yadav maintained that the BJP had little to show for its time in office and accused its leadership of wasting time in government.

Article Title: Crowd, rain or misleading announcement: What led to Kolkata stampede tragedy?
Article Text:
Several people reportedly fell down a flight of stairs near the exit and were trampled by those behind them

What we know about Kolkata stampede

Crowd management and security under scrutiny

State orders safety review of pandals

NEW DELHI: A sudden surge of people, heavy rain and alleged confusion over announcements and entry-exit routes are among the factors being investigated after a stampede at the Chorbagan Sarbojanin Durga Puja pandal in Kolkata killed at least 19 people and injured 25 others on Saturday evening.The incident occurred around 7.15pm on Maha Saptami, when a large crowd waiting on the narrow Radha Madhab Saha Lane to enter the pandal reportedly surged forward as a downpour began. Those already inside were caught in the rush, with people unable to move towards the exit as visitors ahead blocked their way. Several people reportedly fell down a flight of stairs near the exit and were trampled by those behind them.A misleading announcement by the puja committee is also suspected to have added to the confusion, while the blowing of whistles by private security guards may have triggered a rush among visitors, according to CM Adhikari.Kolkata Police are investigating whether lapses in crowd management, confusion over entry and exit routes, and heavy rain contributed to the tragedy, a senior officer told PTI. Eyewitnesses alleged that announcements about entry, exit and crowd movement were improper, leaving visitors confused during peak hours.Locals also questioned the police deployment at the venue, claiming that personnel were largely stationed near the VIP entrance."I have not seen adequate police presence this year. This resulted in the mismanagement," Chorbagan resident Sanghamitra Bhowmik told PTI.Another concern raised by locals was the alleged lack of administrative assistance in taking the injured to hospitals."There must be some lapses, but these should be probed. Whether lapses were on the part of the organisers or they had flouted the rules to erect the pandal will be checked," the police officer told PTI.A forensic team visited the site late on Saturday to collect evidence. Police are questioning the organisers and examining CCTV footage, while also seeking details of the security guards and other personnel deployed to manage the crowd. Officers who were posted at the venue will also be questioned as part of the investigation.Adhikari, who visited the injured at Kolkata Medical College and Hospital, said the incident had raised concerns about safety arrangements at crowded Durga Puja venues. According to hospital sources, 11 injured people were shifted to SSKM Hospital. The deceased included 13 women and a child, a source at the medical college said.The chief minister announced a high-level committee to inspect prominent pandals across West Bengal and review crowd management, exit routes, lighting and structural safety. The panel will be led by Disaster Management Principal Secretary Rajesh Sinha, Fire Services Director General Anuj Sharma and Additional Director General of Police (Law and Order) Javed Shamim.Adhikari urged organisers to follow official safety recommendations, warning against elaborate themes that compromise visitors' safety. He also called for wider exits, better lighting and the removal of bottlenecks created by temporary rope enclosures. Where complex structures obstruct movement, organisers may be advised to restrict rituals to the inner sanctum and use LED screens outside.The state government has announced Rs 25 lakh in compensation and a Group D government job for the family of each deceased victim. A toll-free helpline, 18003455678, has also been set up to help people seeking information about those affected.
Article Summary: A stampede at a Durga Puja pandal in Kolkata killed at least 19 people and injured 25 others on Saturday evening. Police are investigating whether lapses in crowd management, confusion over entry and exit routes, and heavy rain contributed to the tragedy. Eyewitnesses alleged that announcements about entry, exit and crowd movement were improper.

Article Title: Lucknow Police double reward for information on absconding model Shraddha Dubey to Rs 50,000
Article Text:
Police have doubled the reward for information leading to Dubey’s arrest from 25,000 to 50,000.





LUCKNOW: Shraddha Dubey, the prime accused in the death of 28-year-old Shiva Sharma , surfaced publicly for the first time in a brief video interview on Sunday, denying allegations of murder even as she remained untraceable to Lucknow Police, who say they are pursuing multiple leads including a suspected Nepal link.Her appearance came amid speculation that she would surrender at Hazratganj police station, a development that did not materialise. Instead, Dubey spoke to a news agency from an undisclosed location in a video lasting three minutes and 56 seconds, disputing the accusation that she and others were involved in Sharma’s death.Police have doubled the reward for information leading to Dubey’s arrest from ₹25,000 to ₹50,000. Her current location has not been officially confirmed, and investigators have not said whether the interview yielded actionable information about her whereabouts. In a parallel move, Hazratganj SHO Vikram Singh was removed and sent to the reserve police lines.In the interview, Dubey claimed Sharma died by suicide after jumping from the fourth floor of her building. She questioned why CCTV footage from the premises had not been released, arguing that it could clarify the sequence of events.Police have not responded publicly to her remarks about the CCTV recordings, and the footage has not been made public.Earlier, DCP Central Vikrant Vir said police teams were working to trace the accused and were close to locating them, but declined to share operational details, citing the risk of information reaching those being sought. Police sources said Dubey’s suspected location was traced to Mahimnagar in Nepal and that three teams were sent across the border to pursue leads. A 16-member team has also been involved in the search, with investigators suspecting Dubey, her sister Rashmi, and their driver were frequently changing locations to evade arrest.An SUV registered in Dubey’s name was earlier found abandoned near Rupaidiha, close to the India-Nepal border, strengthening suspicions she may have travelled in that direction. Police, however, have not publicly established her movements after the vehicle’s recovery.Sharma died on Oct 9 after falling from the fourth floor of a building near Ballu Adda in Lucknow’s Hazratganj area. His mother, Rachna Sharma, accused Dubey and others of involvement, following which a case was registered under Section 103(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.Dubey rejected claims made by Sharma’s mother and denied that a diary had revealed incriminating details. She also objected to photographs of her with different people circulating on social media and said her sister had no knowledge of the incident.Dubey said she had known Sharma for about four months and claimed he was under financial stress, with debts of ₹16-17 lakh and creditors calling him. She alleged he took jewellery worth ₹5-6 lakh from her residence about a month before his death and promised in a video to return it. These assertions have not been independently verified.Explaining why she left while Sharma was being taken to hospital, Dubey said she had breathing difficulties and personal reasons, and claimed her driver fled after being assaulted. She appealed for a fair investigation, stating no one should be declared guilty before the probe concludes. Police have not confirmed her location or reported her arrest.
Article Summary: Shraddha Dubey, the prime accused in the death of 28-year-old Shiva Sharma, surfaced publicly for the first time in a brief video interview on Sunday. Her appearance came amid speculation that she would surrender at Hazratganj police station, a development that did not materialise. Her current location has not been officially confirmed, and investigators have not said whether the interview yielded actionable information about her whereabouts.

Article Title: City halls torched, shops looted: France in shock after violent protest - videos
Article Text:
Chaos, loot and fire as France burns amidst widespread unrest

Macron vows action as arrests mount

City halls set ablaze, businesses looted

Political blame and economic concerns

France witnessed widespread destruction, looting and clashes with police as nationwide protests over the rising cost of living and poor conditions in schools escalated into violence, leaving businesses damaged and public buildings in flames. President Emmanuel Macron has vowed legal action against rioters while announcing measures to address public grievances.The scale of the unrest was visible in Paris on Sunday, where shattered shopfronts, broken glass and dislodged cobblestones littered the area around Place de la République. Videos across social media sites also showed damage and looting in other shopping and tourist districts.Authorities estimated that around 5,50,000 people took part in Saturday’s demonstrations, while organisers put the turnout at 8,00,000. The protests were backed by labour unions, student organisations and activists seeking to revive the “yellow vest” movement, which emerged in 2018 over social injustice.In a televised address, Macron acknowledged the public’s “anger” and “shame” over the unrest, while drawing a distinction between peaceful demonstrators and those involved in violence.“Those who looted will have to pay for the damage, and those who sought to bring down the Republic will be held accountable,” Macron said.He also condemned what he described as “unrestrained violence” by “insurrectionist elements from radical far-left groups, joined by numerous criminals.”Social media has been flooded with viral videos of burning buildings, smashed storefronts and clashes, with users declaring “France has fallen” and warning that the country is on the brink.At least 2,400 people were arrested, according news agency AP. Macron said he had instructed prefects to work with mayors to protect public buildings and businesses, including by banning protests where necessary.In Limoges, flames engulfed the 19th-century City Hall on Saturday, causing its roof to collapse and nearly destroying the building. Haute-Vienne prefect Maurice Barate said “radical troublemakers” had broken in while officials, employees, security personnel and members of the public were inside.“They deliberately set the building on fire. It is an extremely serious and unspeakable act,” Barate said.In Marseille, protesters briefly entered the City Hall lobby, while a group damaged a police station. In Lyon, a fire broke out inside a tourist office.Paris mayor Emmanuel Grégoire described the damage as “considerable and unprecedented”, while stressing that the capital must remain a place where people can demonstrate and businesses can operate safely.The unrest has also fuelled political tensions ahead of next spring’s presidential election. Far-right leader Marine Le Pen criticised Macron’s government, while left-wing leader Jean-Luc Mélenchon condemned looting and destruction.US president Donald Trump posted “France is burning!” on Truth Social, blaming immigration fro the protets and called on the country to “Close your Borders and take control, before it is too late!” French authorities have not linked immigrants to the rioting.The unrest also weighed on the euro in Asian trading on Monday. The currency fell 0.1% to $1.1225, while the dollar index held at 101.83, Reuters reported.
Article Summary: France witnesses widespread destruction, looting and clashes with police. President Emmanuel Macron has vowed legal action against rioters. The scale of the unrest was visible in Paris on Sunday, where shattered shopfronts, broken glass and dislodged cobblestones littered area around Place de la République.

NEW DELHI: US secretary of State Marco Rubio reiterated that president Donald Trump wants Russia and Ukraine to focus on ending their four-year-old war. The WSJ report said the initiative could allow Moscow to seek a settlement favourable to its interests, while raising concerns in Kyiv and among Washington's European allies over Ukraine's absence from discussions about its own conflict.Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov confirmed to the newspaper that discussions about a possible meeting were underway, but said no final decision had been taken.“There is no clear understanding yet regarding the meeting itself or its potential agenda, although all three parties acknowledge the hypothetical possibility of such a meeting taking place,” Peskov told the WSJ. Article Title: ‘Want to try your luck again?’: Iran’s Araghchi warning to Trump against renewed war
Article Text:
“Last time you wanted to ‘finish the job’, Iran emerged even stronger.

Trump throws weight behind Netanyahu

Iranian foreign minister Abbas Araghchi has issued a sharp warning to US President Donald Trump over his threat to “finish the job” against Tehran, saying Iran came out stronger from the previous confrontation.“Last time you wanted to ‘finish the job’, Iran emerged even stronger. Want to try your luck again? Be our guest. But be careful, we have unfinished jobs too,” Araghchi wrote on X.Taking aim at Netanyahu, the Iranian minister alleged that the Israeli leader was trying to pull the United States into another military conflict to avoid facing legal consequences at home. He cautioned that the fallout could affect both Israel and Trump.“Netanyahu is driving America into another war to stay out of jail, whatever the consequences for Israel—let alone POTUS,” Araghchi said.The exchange followed Trump's public endorsement of Netanyahu ahead of Israel's October 27 parliamentary election. The US president praised the Israeli leader's handling of the confrontation with Iran and his role in pursuing peace.In a lengthy post on Truth Social addressed to the “Great People of Israel”, Trump called Netanyahu a “Great Warrior Prime Minister” and announced his “Complete and Total Endorsement” of his re-election campaign.Also Read: Putin proposes trilateral summit with Trump, Xi to discuss Ukraine war: Report Trump also warned Israeli voters against choosing a different leader, suggesting that the United States might have to intervene if they picked the “wrong Leader”.“I am not inclined to do so,” he added.Trump has accused Iran of posing a threat to both Israel and the United States for decades, pointing to slogans such as “Death to Israel, Death to America”. He warned that Tehran could eventually act on those threats.Claiming that Iran had suffered significant military and financial setbacks, Trump said Washington would “soon finish the job” unless the country changed course quickly.
Article Summary: Iranian foreign minister Abbas Araghchi has issued a sharp warning to US President Donald Trump over his threat to “finish the job” against Tehran. He said Iran came out stronger from the previous confrontation. The exchange followed Trump's public endorsement of Netanyahu ahead of Israel's October 27 parliamentary election.

Article Title: Foreigner alleges rape by man she met online in Goa
Article Text:
The survivor, a divorcee, is European and had subsequently acquired another country’s nationality.

(The victim's identity has not been revealed to protect her privacy as per Supreme court directives on cases related to sexual assault)





PANAJI: Goa police have registered an FIR against a man for allegedly raping a 45-year-old foreign tourist at the coastal village of Mandrem.Police said the survivor got in touch with the accused on social media and made plans to meet in Goa.The survivor, a divorcee, is European and had subsequently acquired another country’s nationality. Police said that as the woman was under the influence of alcohol, she could not resist when the accused person sexually assaulted her.Police said the incident was initially reported at Mandrem police station, but subsequently shifted to the women police station in Panaji, as there was no proper coordination between Mandrem police and the survivor.Goa police statistics reveal that on average, the state sees four women raped or sexually assaulted every week. From 2021 to 2025, a total of 922 women—aged between five and 70—were either raped or sexually assaulted.Police said that higher reporting and registration of offences in Goa reflect greater public awareness, easier access to police mechanisms, and increased public confidence in approaching law enforcement agencies.
Article Summary: Goa police have registered an FIR against a man for allegedly raping a 45-year- old foreign tourist at the coastal village of Mandrem. Article Title: ‘Jaldi le kar jaao, Tiger’: Video shows seat switch as Tiger Shroff takes the wheel after attack
Article Text:
Tiger Shroff switched places with his injured driver to expedite his hospital transfer

Lawrence Bishnoi gang claims responsibility for Tiger Shroff attack





MUMBAI: Bollywood actor Tiger Shroff reportedly took the wheel and rushed his injured driver to hospital after unidentified assailants opened fire at his car in Mumbai’s Juhu area on Sunday evening.A video of the incident shows the actor switching seats with his driver after the firing. A woman can be heard saying, “Jaldi le kar jaao, Tiger”.Blood stains are also visible in the aftermath of the attack.Shroff’s driver, Firdaus, sustained a gunshot wound to his left hand, while the actor escaped without any bullet injuries. The incident took place near Pushpa Narsee Park, where the actor’s vehicle was targeted by motorcycle-borne assailants.Another person, an autorickshaw driver, was also injured in the firing, according to police.The video shows Shroff moving into the driver's seat after his driver was injured in the shooting. The actor reportedly took charge of the vehicle to get the injured driver medical attention.Shroff and Firdaus were taken to Nanavati Hospital in Vile Parle. Doctors said the actor had sustained minor abrasions but no bullet wounds, while the driver suffered a gunshot injury to his left hand.The other injured person, an autorickshaw driver identified as Chauhan, was taken to Cooper Hospital with bullet injuries to his chest.The firing took place around 7 pm on Sunday near Pushpa Narsee Park in Juhu, when Shroff was returning in his car. Seven shots were fired in all.Unidentified assailants allegedly opened fire at the vehicle, injuring the driver and another person nearby.Police have launched an investigation and formed multiple teams to identify and apprehend those involved. CCTV footage from the area is being examined, while forensic teams have begun analysing evidence collected from the spot.Anil Pandit and Harman Sandhu, purportedly associated with the Lawrence Bishnoi gang, claimed responsibility for the firing in a social media post and a voice note.The message also threatened people in the Mumbai film industry who work with actor Salman Khan.The authenticity of the claims and their alleged connection to the shooting had not been independently established, and police were investigating the motive behind the attack.Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis spoke to Mumbai Police Commissioner Deven Bharti and directed the police to expedite the investigation and take strict action against those responsible. Fadnavis also spoke to Shroff and assured him, “We are all with you. We will trace and apprehend the accused at the earliest.”
Article Summary: Bollywood actor Tiger Shroff reportedly took the wheel and rushed his injured driver to hospital. Unidentified assailants opened fire at his car in Mumbai’s Juhu area on Sunday evening. A video of the incident shows the actor switching seats with his driver after the firing.

Article Title: Man stripped, beaten with belts, petrol poured on private parts; video of assault goes viral
